summary.headline: Century Enka Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to Rs 558 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.88% and PAT dropped 17% YoY to Rs 19 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 37% YoY to Rs 558 crore in Q2 FY27, with volume up 13% YoY to 20,162 MT, largely on higher raw material-led realisations. EBITDA rose 4% YoY to Rs 33 crore but margin compressed to 5.88% (down 186 bps YoY and 958 bps QoQ) as raw material volatility, a normalising low-cost opening inventory benefit and higher grid power and LNG costs weighed. H1 FY27 revenue rose 37% to Rs 1,113 crore, EBITDA rose 130% to Rs 119 crore and PAT rose 113% to Rs 80 crore. Imports hit tyre cord fabric (NTCF) sales volume in Q2, while PTCF commercial sales are slated to start in Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +4% YoY; margin -186 bps YoY, -958 bps QoQ from 15.46%

segments.name: Tyre cord fabric (NTCF)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales Rs 251 crore (+37% YoY); H1 Rs 557 crore (+53% YoY). Imports booked in Q1 as risk mitigation weighed on Q2 volumes; management expects normalisation in coming quarters but flagged possible import spikes.

segments.name: Nylon filament yarn
segments.commentary: Q2 sales Rs 293 crore (+39% YoY); H1 Rs 523 crore (+30% YoY). Volumes improved on festive demand, but margins constrained by low-priced Chinese imports in base and low-grade yarn.

segments.name: PTCF (polyester tyre cord fabric)
segments.commentary: Not yet commercial. Approval process progressing; commercial sales expected from Q4 FY27, with gradual ramp-up and high utilisation expected in H2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin target range of 7% to 10%; management said Q2 (5.88%) is below its normal operating range.
PTCF commercial sales to commence in Q4 FY27; ramp-up gradual given multi-stage passenger car tyre approvals.
Hybrid power capacity additions at Bharuch expected to start delivering from Q4 FY27, with rough annualised benefit of about Rs 10 crore from the additional hybrid capacity.
Mother Yarn expansion at Pune expected to be capitalised in FY28.
Value-added products (VAPs) share of nylon filament yarn expected to reach about 50% in the near term.
Management declined to give formal forward-looking revenue or volume guidance, citing demand and raw material uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity approximately 92,000 MT; utilisation about 85% in Q2 FY27, with management guiding a 80% to 90% range depending on demand.
Ongoing CWIP projects: Mother Yarn expansion at Pune, increase in VAP capacity at Bharuch, energy-saving capex at both locations, safety improvements and old asset replacement.
Capital WIP rose from about Rs 13 crore in FY26 to about Rs 38 crore in H1 FY27.
Nylon capacity expansion completed in the quarter to support higher-margin offerings; no further nylon capacity expansion needed per management.
Polyester capacity is available but awaiting customer approvals (pool process); utilisation expected from Q4 FY27 onwards and mainly in FY28.
Capital allocation: company is not constrained by cash; capex approved through board on merit criteria.
demand_pricing: OEM tyre demand described as robust through September, with tractor sales the exception; secondary/replacement market weaker per ATMA data, with monsoon a factor.
Festive-season demand and the GST reduction (since September last year) cited as demand supports.
Raw material volatility sharply higher in Q2 due to Iran war; caprolactam about USD 2,000 to 2,100/t and nylon chips about USD 2,100 to 2,200/t currently.
Management says price increases were passed through, with timing gaps; absolute Q2 profit said to be above prior-year level.
Import competition from China in base and low-grade nylon yarn pressured margins; imports in Q1 were booked by tyre companies as risk mitigation.
Exports only 4% to 5% of turnover; EU and UK FTAs seen as future opportunities. Nuenyl (recycled yarn) targeted at export brands; Enkalon remains a domestic premium brand.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 37% revenue growth and how sustainable are realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to volume growth plus higher realisations driven by raw material prices (caprolactam and polymerised chips). It said future pricing is very hard to project given high Q1 and Q2 volatility, which was much higher in Q2 due to the Iran war.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hybrid power benefit and how much headroom is there in capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The additional hybrid power is expected from Q4 FY27 with a rough annualised benefit of about Rs 10 crore. Utilisation was about 85% in Q2 and is expected to range 80% to 90%, with sufficient headroom for short-term demand surges.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NTCF sales fall due to imports and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tyre companies booked larger imports in Q1 as a risk-mitigation step amid gas and raw material uncertainty. Management expects normalisation in coming quarters, but import spikes could recur in a volatile quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin sustainable and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a normalised EBITDA margin of 7% to 10%. Q1 was exceptional due to low-cost opening inventory and Q2 was below normal range given rising raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added product share in yarn and how does it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: VAP share is rising quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year and is expected to reach about 50% in the near term. Management said VAP growth is already contributing to yarn margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: How is inventory rising and how will working capital evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose to about Rs 313 crore at end-H1, mainly because of higher raw material prices; volumes in quantity terms were flat to lower. Working capital should normalise when raw material prices move.

risks_watch: Raw material (caprolactam, nylon chips) price volatility linked to crude and the Iran war; timing gaps in pass-through to customers.
Continued Chinese and other imports pressuring NTCF volumes and base nylon yarn margins.
Weaker secondary/replacement tyre demand if monsoon, inflation or interest rates worsen.
Bharuch grid power tariffs and LNG prices; hybrid power benefit timing from Q4 FY27.
PTCF approval timeline and ramp-up pace; polyester capacity awaiting customer approvals.
Q3 margin recovery toward the 7% to 10% target range; inventory and working capital unwinding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand fundamentals and product diversification (PTCF, VAPs, hybrid power) but cautious and at times evasive on pricing, margins and demand outlook, citing geopolitical and crude volatility. Management repeatedly declined to give forward numbers or segment-level breakups for competitive reasons.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 was exceptional because we benefited from the low-cost inventory and post-war there was a significant price increase in crude and all the crude derivative raw materials.
So, normally our target would be between 7% to 10%.
We expect on a very rough calculation basis, annualized benefit of about Rs. 10 crores per annum.
we expect to commence commercial sales in Q4 FY27.

adds.what: PTCF (polyester tyre cord fabric) polyester capacity, available but awaiting customer approvals; commercial sales from Q4 FY27
Hybrid power capacity additions at Bharuch, expected to deliver from Q4 FY27 (~Rs 10 cr annualised benefit)
Mother Yarn expansion at Pune, expected to be capitalised in FY28

growth.why: Management declined formal revenue or volume guidance; it reiterated a normalised 7-10% EBITDA margin target (Q2 at 5.88% below range), utilisation ~85% with 80-90% guided range, and PTCF commercial sales from Q4 FY27 plus Pune Mother Yarn capitalisation in FY28, with no further nylon capacity needed.
